newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CPFL demand rose 5.4 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CPFL demand rose 5.4 pct in Sept.

text.p: Brazilian state power firm Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) said electrical energy demand rose 5.4 percent in September versus the same month last year due mostly to an on-going recovery in industry.
CPFL, a power distributor owned by Sao Paulo state, said in a statement that consumption was up 6.5 percent to in the January-September period compared with the same nine-month period in 1995.
"The result stemmed from higher demand in the industrial sector, which since May has shown signs of recovery," the firm said.
It said industrial power consumption, which accounts for 45 percent of CPFL's market, was up 8.9 percent in September compared with the same month last year and 4.8 percent in the nine-month period.
CPFL said residential usage was up 4.9 percent last month while commercial consumption climbed 5.3 percent versus September 1995.
Total consumption of power reached 1,502,289 megawatts in September and 12,350,179 megawatt in the nine-month period, it said.
